blocks.text: **Human rights** are the inherent, universal rights of all persons, protected in India through the **Constitution (Fundamental Rights), the Protection of Human Rights Act (1993), and the NHRC/SHRCs**, and globally through the **UDHR and UN mechanisms**.

rows: **Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR, 1948)**; ICCPR & ICESCR covenants.
**Fundamental Rights (Part III)**; **Protection of Human Rights Act (1993)**.
Statutory; chaired by a former **CJI or SC judge**; recommendatory powers; investigates violations.
**Custodial violence, recommendatory (not binding) powers, delays, armed-forces exemption**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: human rights & mechanisms

items: **Global**: **UDHR (1948)**; twin covenants **ICCPR & ICESCR (1966)**; UN Human Rights Council (Geneva); India is a party to major conventions.
**India**: **Protection of Human Rights Act (1993)** → **NHRC** (Chair = former CJI/SC judge) & **SHRCs**; deals with custodial deaths, atrocities, etc. — but **recommendatory** & 1-year limitation.
**Constitutional basis**: FRs (Part III), DPSP, PILs, writ jurisdiction; **Art 21** as the fount of many rights (privacy, dignity, clean environment, health).
**Vulnerable-group commissions**: NCW, NCPCR, NCSC/NCST/NCBC, NCM (minorities); **UN mechanisms** — UNHRC UPR of India.
UDHR (1948); NHRC (1993, statutory) — recommendatory powers only; headed by ex-CJI/SC judge.
Protection of Human Rights Act 1993 = the enabling law.

blocks.text: Women's rights in India are protected by **constitutional guarantees, a body of protective legislation, and institutions like the National Commission for Women** — reinforced by **reservation in local bodies** and recent measures against violence and for empowerment.

rows: **Equality (14-15), no discrimination, Art. 15(3) special provisions, Art. 39(d) equal pay, 42 maternity relief, 243D/T (⅓ reservation in local bodies)**.

**Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (106th Amendment, 2023)** — ⅓ seats in Lok Sabha & assemblies (on delimitation).
**Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, PM Matru Vandana, Ujjwala, One Stop Centres**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: women's rights & protections

blocks.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes enjoy a comprehensive framework of **constitutional safeguards — social, economic, political, educational and service** — plus special protective laws and national commissions, aimed at ending historic discrimination and ensuring social justice.

rows: **Reservation of seats (Arts. 330, 332)** in Lok Sabha & assemblies; local bodies.
**Fifth & Sixth Schedules, PESA (1996), Forest Rights Act (2006)**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: SC/ST rights & safeguards

items: **Constitutional**: **Art 17** (untouchability abolished), **Art 15(4)/16(4)** (reservation), **Art 46** (DPSP — educational/economic promotion), **Art 335** (services), **Art 338/338A** (NCSC/NCST), **Art 330/332** (reserved seats), **Fifth & Sixth Schedules** (tribal administration).

**Laws**: **SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989** (amended 2018 — no anticipatory bail; special courts), **PCR Act 1955**, **Forest Rights Act 2006** (individual & community forest rights for STs & OTFDs), **PESA 1996**.
**Reservation**: SC ~15%, ST ~7.5%, OBC 27%, **EWS 10% (103rd Amendment 2019)**; the **Indra Sawhney (1992)** cap of 50% & 'creamy layer' for OBCs.
**AP**: agency areas under the Fifth Schedule; ITDAs (Integrated Tribal Development Agencies); Land Transfer Regulation (1/70) protecting tribal land.
Art 17 (untouchability), 330/332 (seat reservation), PoA Act 1989, FRA 2006, PESA 1996.
NCSC (338), NCST (338A) constitutional; 5th/6th Schedules for tribal areas.

blocks.text: **Child rights** in India are protected by **constitutional provisions, a set of dedicated laws (POCSO, RTE, Juvenile Justice, child-labour ban), and the NCPCR** — aligned with the **UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC)**.

rows: **RTE Act (2009), POCSO (2012), Juvenile Justice Act (2015), Child Labour (Prohibition) Act, Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (2006)**.
Statutory body protecting child rights; monitors RTE/POCSO.
**UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC, 1989)** — India ratified 1992.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: child rights & laws

items: **Constitutional**: **Art 21A** (free & compulsory education 6-14, 86th Amendment), Art 24 (no child <14 in hazardous work), Art 39(e)(f), Art 45 (early childhood care), Art 51A(k) (parents' duty to educate).

**Laws**: **RTE Act 2009**, **POCSO Act 2012** (child sexual offences; gender-neutral), **Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection) Act 2015** (16-18 for heinous crimes; adoption via CARA), **Child Labour (Prohibition) Amendment 2016** (banned <14 in all occupations), **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act 2006**.
**Bodies/Schemes**: **NCPCR / SCPCR**, Childline 1098, **ICDS/Anganwadi, Mid-Day Meal (PM POSHAN), Beti Bachao**, Integrated Child Protection Scheme.
**International**: UN **Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989)** — India ratified 1992.
Art 21A (RTE), 24 (child labour); POCSO 2012, RTE 2009, JJ Act 2015; NCPCR 2007.
UNCRC 1989 (India ratified 1992); ICDS/Mid-Day Meal schemes.
